records.title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer.
records.abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti-breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8+ T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)-mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell-mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

records.title: PRR12 variants cause intellectual disability by disrupting neuronal differentiation and maturation.
records.abstract: Mutations in the proline-rich 12 (PRR12) gene cause neurodevelopmental disorders that are mainly characterized by intellectual disability. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identified six pathogenic de novo mutations in PRR12 in unrelated patients with intellectual disability, showing significant enrichment in this cohort (false discovery rate = 0.014). Using both mouse models and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural cultures and cortical organoids, we functionally dissected the underlying mechanism. We found that PRR12 haploinsufficiency impairs cortical neuronal differentiation and neurite outgrowth, thereby contributing to cognitive deficits. Furthermore, we demonstrated that PRR12 is enriched at the promoters of key regulatory genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic transmission, including SNCG. Attenuation of SNCG expression rescued the PRR12 haploinsufficiency-associated neuronal structure and dendritic spine defects, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue in children with PRR12-related intellectual disability. Collectively, our findings elucidate the mechanism by which PRR12 haploinsufficiency contributes to intellectual disability and provide insights into potential therapeutic strategies.

records.title: An epithelium-intrinsic zinc sensor maintains gut homeostasis by regulating Paneth and tuft cell differentiation.
records.abstract: Zinc (Zn) is an essential micronutrient required for cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis, yet how epithelial Zn sensing governs the constantly renewing intestinal barrier remains unclear. We disrupted Zn homeostasis by deleting metal response element-binding transcription factor-1 (MTF1), a Zn-sensitive master regulator of intracellular metal homeostasis, specifically in intestinal epithelial cells (MTF1ΔIEC). This allowed us to probe how impaired Zn sensing affects epithelial function. MTF1ΔIEC mice showed altered metal homeostasis, heightened sensitivity to dietary Zn, and exaggerated inflammatory profile. Loss of MTF1 depleted Paneth and tuft cell lineages, weakening epithelial defenses against commensal and pathogenic microbes. Using cell type-specific and inducible MTF1 deletion with lineage tracing, we show that MTF1-dependent Zn homeostasis was required for differentiation rather than lineage persistence. Organoids derived from MTF1ΔIEC mice confirmed that loss of MTF1 increases proliferation while reducing tuft and Paneth cells in a Zn-dependent manner, underscoring the role of Zn in maintaining intestinal immune homeostasis.

records.title: Potential roles of selected bioactive polysaccharides in intestinal stem-cell-mediated epithelial renewal: a narrative review.
records.abstract: The intestinal epithelium is continuously renewed by intestinal stem cells located within specialized crypt niches. Although bioactive polysaccharides are widely studied for their effects on barrier integrity, inflammation, mucus production, and gut microbiota composition, their potential roles in stem-cell-mediated epithelial renewal remain poorly defined. This narrative review summarizes current evidence linking selected dietary polysaccharides to intestinal stem-cell regulation. Available studies suggest that resistant starch, inulin, β-glucans, glucomannan, pectins, fucans, and human milk oligosaccharides may influence crypt proliferation, stem-cell-marker expression, lineage allocation, organoid growth, and epithelial repair in experimental models. Mechanistically, these effects may involve microbiota-dependent pathways, including short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-derived indoles, bile acid metabolites, and IL-22-related immune signaling, as well as microbiota-independent epithelial or injury-adaptive pathways. However, evidence remains largely preclinical, heterogeneous, and often correlative. Regenerative outcomes appear to depend on polysaccharide structure, fermentation kinetics, crypt-level metabolite gradients, host context, and injury timing. Future studies should prioritize intestinal stem-cell-related endpoints, chemically defined polysaccharides, causal pathway validation, spatial metabolite profiling, and organoid systems incorporating microbial, immune, and stromal niche components.

records.title: DNA Damage Repair Systems in 5-Fluorouracil Resistance of Colorectal Cancer: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Intervention Strategies.
records.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent for colorectal cancer; however, primary and acquired resistance remain major barriers to effective 5-FU-based therapy. The review focuses on evidence linking DDR alterations to 5-FU response or resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC) and frames the literature according to molecular context, direct versus extrapolated evidence, and preclinical, exploratory clinical, or established clinical status. 5-FU induces cytotoxic stress through multiple mechanisms, including thymidylate synthase inhibition, disruption of nucleotide metabolism, incorporation of uracil and fluorinated metabolites into DNA, and induction of DNA damage and replication stress. Adaptive alterations in major DNA damage response (DDR) components, including mismatch repair (MMR), base excision repair (BER), homologous recombination (HR), non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), and DNA polymerase theta-mediated end joining (TMEJ), together with context-dependent contributions from nucleotide excision repair (NER)-associated factors, may enable tumor cells to repair or tolerate DNA lesions and sustain survival under therapeutic pressure. DDR-related targets, including PARP, APE1, POLQ, WRN, ATR, CHK1, and WEE1, have emerged as potential therapeutic targets for enhancing 5-FU sensitivity in selected molecular contexts. Translational approaches, including immunotherapy, organoid-based drug sensitivity testing, circulating tumor DNA monitoring, and single-cell and spatial omics, provide complementary tools for investigating biomarker-guided treatment strategies and resistance evolution. This review examines how DDR alterations contribute to 5-FU resistance in colorectal cancer and evaluates DDR-related therapeutic vulnerabilities with emphasis on molecular context, strength of evidence, biomarker stratification, and translational challenges.

records.title: Hydrogen-associated CXCL2 drives adaptive inflammatory-to-proliferative state transition during skin wound healing.
records.abstract: Wound healing is an environmentally adaptive process. It requires a tightly coordinated transition from an inflammatory to a proliferative state, which occurs in response to oxidative and inflammatory stress. Molecular hydrogen (H2) is a widely recognized medical gas, and it alleviates oxidative stress and selectively eliminates highly cytotoxic reactive oxygen species. However, it remains unclear whether redox-active gases such as H2 can actively orchestrate tissue state transitions, rather than merely mitigating oxidative damage. Bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses were integrated to investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying H2-mediated wound healing. Functional studies were performed in hydrogen-mediated mouse skin injury models and in self-assembled skin organoid models. Immunofluorescence staining, Masson's trichrome staining, and qRT-PCR were used to validate key signaling pathways and assess tissue regeneration, angiogenesis, and wound healing outcomes. H2 significantly accelerated wound healing, especially during the proliferative phase, where it acted as a critical regulator of the inflammatory-to-proliferative transition. Multi-omics analyses identified a hydrogen-associated macrophage program and revealed a CXCL2-ACKR1 signaling axis mediating macrophage-endothelial communication. Functional validation confirmed that activation of this axis promoted endothelial migration, angiogenesis, and granulation tissue formation. As a result, the transition from inflammation to proliferation was facilitated, and wound closure was accelerated. H2 spatiotemporally coordinates adaptive wound healing by regulating a macrophage-endothelial CXCL2-ACKR1 signaling axis that drives the inflammatory-to-proliferative transition. These findings provide mechanistic insight into how H2 spatiotemporally coordinates adaptive wound healing and highlight the potential of hydrogen-mediated redox modulation as a mechanism for regulating tissue repair.

records.title: A Testable Framework for Mechanics-Conditioned Perturbation Models in Drug Discovery.
records.abstract: Perturbation-predictive cell models are advancing quickly, yet they remain predominantly molecular, even though the mechanical state of cells and tissues-stiffness, viscoelasticity, geometry, and force generation-can alter therapeutic response. This review converts that observation into a testable program. It separates four claims that are routinely conflated and gives each its own baseline, estimand, design, and named refutation condition: whether auxiliary mechanical measurements improve prediction of treatment response beyond a complete non-mechanical baseline (H1); whether mechanics computed from images help as a representation rather than as added information (H2); whether experimentally controlled mechanical context modifies treatment effects, including once local drug exposure is held comparable (H3 and H3a); and whether mechanics-aware predictions improve preclinical prioritization decisions under a fixed budget (H4). Current evidence is graded against an explicit, reproducible rubric, and the two links the framework actually requires, mechanical conditioning of perturbation response and prospectively validated mechanics-aware decisions, are unpopulated. A worked pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma program specifies donors, materials, gemcitabine exposure measurement, endpoints, simulation-based power, staged costs, and a blinded decision test, with a reduced-scope minimum implementation for groups that cannot execute the full design. The practical contribution for a bioengineering readership is a transferable specification checklist, covering measurement provenance, units of assignment and inference, leakage control, effect margins, and decision rules, to be completed before resources are committed. We conclude that mechanics should enter perturbation models as a hypothesis carrying a refutation condition, not as a default enrichment. Explicit limitations bound the work: the synthesis is targeted rather than systematic, the evidence grades were assigned by a single assessor, and the framework has not itself been executed.

records.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: Current Evidence, Multiscale Modeling Approaches, and Challenges in Clinical Translation-A Narrative Review.
records.abstract: Digital Twin (DT), a dynamic simulation technology derived from the engineering field, has been deeply integrated into the field of tumor precision medicine, empowered by both multi-omics technologies and artificial intelligence. It offers a novel approach to overcoming the limitations of traditional paradigms in tumor research, diagnosis, and treatment. This article reviews the full-scale application system of tumor DT, spanning from the molecular to the individual level, and constructs a progressive simulation architecture of "virtual cell-virtual knockout/virtual overexpression-virtual organoid-virtual patient". The virtual cell enables the in silico representation of tumor cells and the tumor microenvironment, serving as the fundamental unit for dissecting molecular mechanisms. Virtual knockout/overexpression provides non-invasive, high-throughput methods for target prioritization, significantly shortening research and development cycles. The virtual organoid achieves computational reconstruction of the three-dimensional (3D) tumor microenvironment, bridging the gap between single-cell and individual-scale simulations. The virtual patient, in turn, supports personalized therapeutic decision-making and virtual clinical trials. By synthesizing the latest research findings in the field, this article delineates the technical pathways, primary modeling tools, and representative empirical cases for each application tier. It further provides an in-depth analysis of core challenges, including multi-source data heterogeneity, insufficient model accuracy and interpretability, and obstacles to clinical translation. Corresponding solutions, such as data standardization, cross-scale technology integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration between medicine and engineering, are proposed. The aim is to provide a comprehensive reference for leveraging DT to advance tumor research and facilitate its translation into clinical practice.

records.title: SparseKG-Flow: A Virtual Cell Generative Architecture Unifying Structural Causal Models and Knowledge Graph Priors for Single-Cell Drug Perturbation Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting single-cell responses to new drugs is essential for mechanism-aware virtual cell modeling, yet existing models often fail on unseen drugs or cell types by relying on memorized correlations rather than transferable mechanisms. SparseKG-Flow addresses this out-of-distribution (OOD) challenge as a generative architecture integrating three inductive biases: a sparse drug-effect encoder with Gumbel-Softmax gating, a heterogeneous graph adapter for drug-target-pathway knowledge, and a mechanism-guided residual flow decoder. On Tahoe-100M, it achieves Pearson r of 0.942 and 0.920 under Test-NewDrug and Test-NewCell settings, respectively, outperforming the next-best baseline by 16.6% and 14.8%. It also reduces Δ expression error by 89.0% and 91.7%, respectively, and more than doubles held-out-drug top-gene recovery (Overlap@50 = 0.210). Frozen-model evaluation on high-grade serous ovarian cancer patient data provides preliminary evidence of transfer beyond the Tahoe-100M panel. Ablations confirm all components aid OOD generalization, with the molecular knowledge adapter contributing the most. SparseKG-Flow further reorganizes pharmacological priors into interpretable, task-trained representations and highlights Abemaciclib, Capmatinib, and Gemcitabine in A549 analysis. It thus serves as both an accurate perturbation predictor and a mechanism-grounded virtual cell platform for therapeutic prioritization.

records.title: MitoLODE: a virtual mitochondrion framework with knowledge graph priors for trajectory modeling and mechanistic perturbation analysis.
records.abstract: Mitochondria play a central role in the pathogenesis of major diseases. Tracking how they evolve under disease conditions is valuable for understanding pathological mechanisms and identifying intervention windows. Existing single-cell trajectory inference methods rely on pseudotime rather than a real temporal axis, and rarely model disease and control as independent trajectories. Virtual cell methods target one-shot drug perturbation responses and do not handle the continuous temporal evolution of disease phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose a virtual mitochondrion research paradigm. We first curate and construct MitoKG, a mitochondria-specific heterogeneous knowledge graph integrated from five authoritative databases. MitoKG contains 2549 nodes of four types and 23 019 edges of five relation types. Building on these priors, we develop MitoLODE, a conditioned dual-trajectory neural ordinary differential equation framework. MitoLODE embeds graph priors and temporal features throughout encoding, continuous-time dynamics, and decoding, modeling disease and control evolution as two coupled paths. Benchmarked against eight baselines across four datasets covering Parkinson's disease, cardiac, and pancreatic differentiation, MitoLODE leads in most settings and remains robust under low-data regimes and extrapolation to unseen time points. Two synthetic datasets with known ground truth validate its trajectory recovery under controlled conditions. Building on the trained model, we design a gradient-guided perturbation procedure that identifies potential intervention targets aligned with known Parkinson's pathology. We develop MGMI, a large language model-based reasoning module that grounds model outputs in MitoKG nodes and turns them into confidence-graded mechanistic hypotheses, which nonetheless require experimental validation.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: FLAb2: Benchmarking reveals that protein AI models cannot yet consistently predict developability properties.
records.abstract: We introduce the Fitness Landscape for Antibodies (FLAb2), the largest public benchmark for therapeutic antibody design, comprising developability data for over 4 million antibodies across 32 studies and covering 7 properties: thermostability, expression, aggregation, binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, polyreactivity, and immunogenicity. Evaluating 30 AI and biophysical models, we find that most (80%) fail to produce statistically significant correlations. No model performs well across all properties. Some pretrained models (IgLM, ProGen2, Chai-1, ESM2, ISM, and IgFold) show significant zero-shot correlations for select properties. Fine-tuning with ≥102 points helps for thermostability, aggregation, and binding though polyreactivity and pharmacokinetics lack sufficient data. With enough data (103 points), a fine-tuned one-hot encoding model matches billion-parameter models. Training data matters more than architecture, and intrinsic properties (thermostability) are predicted more readily than extrinsic ones (immunogenicity and pharmacokinetics). Partial correlation analysis shows that germline distance accounts for ∼37% of language models' apparent predictive power.

records.title: EvoSeq: A Eukaryotic Sequence-Function Profiling Platform for AI-Guided Engineering of Genome-Editing Enzymes.
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping protein engineering, yet progress remains constrained by the limited availability of scalable, normalized sequence-activity datasets and experimental benchmarks. Reported here is Evolution by Sequencing (EvoSeq), a sequencing-based profiling platform for genome-editing enzymes that links each variant to a reporter sequence change, enabling activity and variant sequence to be quantified together by next-generation sequencing. Representative sequencing-assisted workflows either require separate functional assays or were performed in bacteria. EvoSeq performs sequence-activity profiling in eukaryotic yeast system with reduced background by up to 95-fold compared to bacterial system, positioning EvoSeq as a pooled eukaryotic alternative to workflows that require separate functional assays and to approaches demonstrated primarily in bacteria. Application to adenine base editor evolution identifies variants with 1.4-fold higher on-target activity at a HBG gene target and threefold lower off-target editing at PCSK9 after mRNA-lipid nanoparticle validation in HepG2 cells. An intron-embedded homologous-recombination recording strategy further enables direct evolution of the large Cas12i nuclease CasY7 and supports active learning, increasing the hit rate of model-nominated mutational windows compared with manual selection. EvoSeq therefore provides an experimental benchmarking method for AI-guided protein-design algorithms and AI-compatible sequence-activity profiling platform for engineering genome editors in eukaryotic cells.

records.title: [Advances in ProteinMPNN-driven protein engineering].
records.abstract: Biomanufacturing is a key pathway for promoting the green transformation of conventional production methods. Its core bottleneck lies in the difficulty of natural enzymes to meet the requirements of industrial applications, necessitating the customized modification of enzyme molecules through protein engineering. Conventional semi-rational design is limited by a narrow sequence search space, heavy reliance on known structural information, and high experimental screening costs, which make it difficult to achieve precise design of industrial-grade enzyme molecules. In recent years, artificial intelligence-based protein design technologies represented by ProteinMPNN have made breakthrough progress and are driving a profound paradigm shift in protein engineering. This article systematically describes the technical principles, workflow, and methodological advantages of ProteinMPNN, compares it with Rosetta and other protein design models, and reviews the research progress of this technology in industrial enzyme engineering and biomanufacturing. On this basis, this article discusses current research hotspots and challenges in industrial application, and provides an outlook on future development directions and prospects for industrial implementation. It is expected to serve as a reference for fundamental research and industrial translation in synthetic biology and protein engineering.

records.title: Modeling Protein Evolution with Generative Models: From Extant Sequence Data to Evolutionary Dynamics.
records.abstract: Protein sequences carry a record of evolutionary history shaped by mutation, selection, drift, and epistasis. Recent generative models trained on homologous sequence families offer a new way to read this record: they define probabilistic landscapes that score sequences, generate viable variants, and capture constraints that are difficult to measure experimentally. In this review, we discuss how such landscapes can be used not only for protein design or mutation-effect prediction, but also for modeling evolutionary dynamics. We focus particularly on Direct Coupling Analysis as an interpretable and experimentally validated framework, while placing it in the broader context of generative sequence modeling. We first describe how generative sequence landscapes are inferred and assessed, then review how they can be coupled to population-genetic or substitution-model dynamics to simulate protein evolution across experimental and phylogenetic timescales. Applications include viral evolution, laboratory drift experiments, historical contingency, entrenchment, epistatic drift over time, and long-term sequence-space exploration. We conclude by discussing open challenges, including score-fitness calibration, phylogenetic structure, codon-level mutation biases, indels, and the integration of experimental data.

records.title: ATC Classification and Scaffold-Split pMIC Prediction for Antibacterial Prioritization.
records.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance requires reproducible computational tools that distinguish antibacterial-drug class membership from measured antibacterial potency. We developed a descriptor-based workflow for Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification (ATC)-based prioritization, exploratory molecular generation, and pMIC prediction. ChEMBL 33 structures were encoded using Mordred descriptors. Fourteen classifiers were used to distinguish 248 systemic antibacterial drugs (ATC J01/J04A) from 2540 non-anti-infective reference drugs. Models were assessed by random, independent, and Bemis-Murcko scaffold splits; An exploratory character-level recurrent neural network was used for molecular generation. Separately, eight regressors modeled Staphylococcus aureus pMIC for 33,505 compounds under a scaffold split. Random forest achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.857 on the random-split test set and 0.775 on the independent validation set. For unseen scaffolds, the MCC was 0.746; after removal of six β-lactam ring descriptors, the MCC was 0.738. Across 25 repeated scaffold splits, the random forest test MCC was 0.774 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.752-0.795), supporting the consistency of scaffold-based performance across partitions. Char-RNN validity was 10.8%; the generated molecules were novel relative to the training set (23/25 were also absent from ChEMBL) and synthesizable. Novelty is reported relative to the training set rather than as absolute chemical-space novelty. XGBoost achieved a scaffold-held-out pMIC R2 = 0.510, RMSE = 0.743 log units, and a Spearman ρ = 0.695. Across 10 repeated scaffold splits, XGBoost R2 was 0.505 (95% CI 0.472-0.537), matching the single-split value. On two independent external tests-a 2019-2022 temporal split and 5090 compounds new in the later ChEMBL 37 release - absolute accuracy was lower (R2 = 0.240 and 0.286) while rank correlation was retained (Spearman ρ = 0.502 and 0.566). These results are consistent with the model being prioritized rather than being used for accurate potency-prediction. The ATC classifier prioritizes structures resembling approved antibacterial drugs rather than establishing measured antibacterial activity. The pMIC model provides scaffold-aware estimates of S. aureus potency; both components require assessment of the applicability domain and experimental validation.

records.title: Plasma-Based Genetic Characterization in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: From Real-World Evidence to Prognostic Stratification.
records.abstract: Plasma next-generation sequencing (NGS) is increasingly used in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (aNSCLC), primarily to detect actionable genetic alterations (AGAs). This study aims to depict its role in a real-world setting and to test a novel support vector machine (SVM) classifier of copy number alteration (CNA) profiles as a new prognostic tool. We retrospectively collected clinico-pathological data from aNSCLC patients undergoing plasma NGS according to clinical practice at the Veneto Institute of Oncology. The primary endpoints were to describe tissue-undetected AGAs and assess the potential prognostic impact of CNA profile binary classification on overall survival (OS). 364 aNSCLC patients consecutively undergoing plasma NGS with a commercial panel were included. New AGAs were found in 61 patients (16.8%). Among 341 cases analyzed by the SVM classifier, 60 (17.6%) had an unstable CNA profile (UCP). UCP patients experienced significantly shorter OS than those with a stable profile (p = 0.026). In multivariable left-truncated Cox regression, UCP confirmed an independent adverse prognostic role both across the full cohort (HR = 1.49, p = 0.021) and within non-oncogene-addicted patients (HR = 1.86, p = 0.002). Plasma NGS confirmed its value in defining a more detailed genetic picture of aNSCLC to guide personalized clinical practice. UCP/SCP binary classification had a prognostic role and can be studied for risk stratification.

records.title: Clinical translation of circulating tumor DNA: technological innovation and future pathways from molecular monitoring to precision decision-making.
records.abstract: As the core technology of liquid biopsy, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is emerging as a promising approach in precision oncology-from static tissue genotyping to dynamic molecular monitoring. Leveraging its unique advantages of non-invasiveness, real-time assessment and repeatable sampling, ctDNA analysis offers incremental value beyond traditional tissue biopsy across key clinical scenarios, including early cancer screening, minimal residual disease (MRD) assessment, treatment response monitoring and resistance mechanism dissection. This review systematically discusses the biological foundations and core technological platforms of ctDNA, with a particular focus on the trade-offs between sensitivity and applicability in tumor-informed versus tumor-naïve strategies. We further summarize the latest clinical evidence for ctDNA across multiple solid tumors, including colorectal cancer, non-small-cell lung cancer and melanoma. Despite its tremendous potential, the clinical translation of ctDNA still faces four major challenges: the sensitivity bottleneck in detecting ultra-low-abundance variants; the "low-shedder" phenotype arising from heterogeneous tumor release; false-positive interference from clonal hematopoiesis; and the lack of end-to-end standardization coupled with cost-effectiveness concerns. Notably, recent studies have revealed a possible "decoupling" between absolute ctDNA levels and relative tumor fraction during dynamic monitoring, highlighting the importance of multi-parameter integrated assessment to avoid clinical misinterpretation. Looking forward, five major trends may shape the evolution of ctDNA technologies. First, a shift towards multi-omics integration-encompassing methylation, fragmentomics and copy number alterations-to construct a panoramic molecular portrait beyond mutation detection. Second, the incorporation of artificial intelligence and machine learning for ultra-low-frequency signal denoising, multimodal data fusion and clonal evolution modeling. Third, the validation of ctDNA-guided clinical decision-making through prospective adaptive trials (e.g., treatment escalation and de-escalation strategies). Fourth, expansion into alternative biofluids such as cerebrospinal fluid and urine to overcome the limitations of blood-based assays. Fifth, reducing testing costs and expanding reimbursement to improve accessibility and equity. In summary, ctDNA analysis is transitioning from research laboratories into routine clinical practice, with the ultimate goal of achieving truly personalized, whole-course cancer management through real-time, non-invasive and panoramic molecular monitoring.

records.title: Exosomal proteins in prostate cancer progression: from mechanisms to diagnostic and therapeutic applications.
records.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains a leading cause of cancer death in men, and the limitations of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing continue to delay diagnosis and confound risk stratification. Exosomes, small extracellular vesicles that can be recovered non-invasively from blood and urine, provide a window onto tumour biology, and the proteins they carry are the most readily measurable of their cargoes for clinical assay development. This review summarises how exosomal proteins sustain four programmes that jointly drive PCa progression: Wnt/β-catenin-dependent metastasis, angiogenesis, immune evasion and the suppression of ferroptosis, the iron-dependent, lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death to which treatment-resistant PCa is vulnerable. Each protein is considered together with its cell of origin, carcinoma cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts or tumour-associated macrophages, because the same molecule can act differently depending on the cell that released it. Key examples include GIPC2, which engages the Wnt co-receptor Fzd7 to activate β-catenin signalling; PGAM1, which binds γ-actin in endothelial cells to promote angiogenesis; exosomal PD-1 and PD-L1, which respectively activate myeloid-derived suppressor cells and suppress CD8+ T cells; and FTH1P8 together with CAF-derived miR-432-5p, which blunt ferroptosis and sustain docetaxel and antiandrogen resistance. The review also covers the diagnostic value of urinary exosomal proteins such as PSMA and PSA, the difference between these protein markers and the RNA-based ExoDx EPI test, and the emerging advances, from GMP-compliant manufacturing and single-vesicle quantification to regulatory guidance, that are beginning to overcome the barriers of isolation heterogeneity, scalability, immunogenicity and regulation.

records.title: Tracking tumor biology in real time: circulating tumor cells in laryngopharyngeal carcinoma.
records.abstract: Laryngopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LPSCC), a subset of head and neck malignancies, reveals different clinical outcomes despite similar staging. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) have emerged as one of the important and promising minimally invasive biomarkers for disease management; however, their clinical utility in LPSCC remains unclear, particularly in resource-limited settings. This prospective observational study was conducted at the State Cancer Institute, a part of a tertiary cancer hospital center in the northernmost region of India, from June 2021 to March 2026. Peripheral blood samples were collected at baseline (n=30) and at 3-month follow-up. The 3-month interval was chosen to assess short-term changes in the study parameters. All enrolled subjects continue to remain under follow-up beyond this period, and data collection is ongoing to capture longer-term outcomes. CTCs were detected and quantified using an EpCAM-based enrichment method with immunofluorescence markers. Associations between CTC counts, clinicopathological variables, treatment response, and disease outcomes were analyzed. Baseline CTCs were detected in 53% of patients, with the majority of the demographic and clinical variables showing insignificant associations with CTC positivity (all P>0.05). At 3 months, 94% of evaluable patients achieved a complete response, while CTC progression was noted in 56% (9/16). P = 0.049). CTC dynamics did not correlate significantly with treatment response or survival outcomes. Nodal involvement, rather than CTC burden, emerged as a stronger predictor of prognosis. At 3 years, overall survival (OS) was 69.0% for the cohort, with no significant difference by CTC status (76.9% vs. 62.5%, P = 0.507); however, nodal involvement was strongly associated with poorer OS (90.0% vs. 22.2%, P = 0.0001). Cancer-specific OS at 3 years was 81.2%, with significantly worse outcomes in patients with CTCs, 68.8% vs. 100% (P = 0.049). CTCs were detectable across both early and locally advanced LPSCC. Although dynamic changes in CTCs were noted, their prognostic significance remains unclear. Larger longitudinal studies are required to validate CTCs as biomarkers and to explore their role in personalized management of LPSCC.

records.title: Non-invasive detection of tissue clonal mosaicism in chronic disease.
records.abstract: Liquid biopsy has transformed our ability to non-invasively interrogate the somatic genome, but its reach has been largely confined to fetal genetics in prenatal testing and tumor genetics in cancer. Clonal mosaicism (CM) pervades non-malignant solid tissues, where somatic driver mutations expand under specific selective pressures and may shape the course of chronic illness. Access to this biology has been limited to invasive tissue biopsies, restricting the field to small cohorts and single time points, and has precluded large-scale, clinically-linked analyses. Here, ultra-sensitive cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing of patients with chronic liver disease revealed genome-wide somatic variants from matched liver biopsies at plasma fractions comparable to those of cancers (10^-4 - 10^-5), with signal corresponding to variants from spatially and phylogenetically related clones. A biopsy-naive targeted panel detected pathogenic variants in chronic liver disease driver genes in 81.5% patients with chronic liver disease, undetectable in controls, with stage-specific enrichment of ACVR2A in early disease and clearance of liver-derived signal following transplant. Extending the framework to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we detect clonal expansions of IBD driver genes in active ulcerative colitis, and observe greater detection in patients with pancolitis versus more localized disease. Together, these results open a new domain for cfDNA genetics beyond cancer and prenatal genetics, the non-invasive interrogation of somatic evolution in chronic disease, and establish a framework for the large-cohort, longitudinal, clinically linked studies of solid-tissue CM that has been inaccessible to the field.

records.title: Circulating six-microRNA signature for diagnosis, prognosis, and surgical monitoring in extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: a multicenter, multi-cohort study.
records.abstract: Robust blood biomarkers for the preoperative diagnosis and perioperative assessment of extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA) are lacking. We aimed to develop and validate plasma microRNA signatures for diagnosing eCCA and to explore their perioperative and prognostic relevance. This multicenter biomarker study included 474 participants and 514 plasma specimens across one derivation, one discovery, three internal validation, and two independent external validation cohorts. Candidate microRNAs were prioritized using small-RNA sequencing and random-forest analysis. Reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction and logistic regression were used to develop a weighted six-microRNA model (Signature I) and an unweighted score (Signature II). Discovery-derived formulas and thresholds were locked before validation. Paired preoperative and postoperative-day-7 samples were used to assess perioperative changes. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for pathological T and N stages, resection-margin status, and tumor differentiation evaluated prognostic associations. Signature I achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.90 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.84-0.97) for distinguishing eCCA from common bile duct stones in both internal and external disease-control cohorts, compared with AUCs of 0.77 and 0.76, respectively, for CA19-9 (DeLong P = 0.041 and P = 0.033, respectively). At the prespecified threshold, its sensitivity and specificity in the external disease-control cohort were 82.5% and 80.0%, respectively. In the external healthy-control cohort, Signature I achieved an AUC of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.81-0.96), while the corresponding AUC for Signature I plus CA19-9 was 0.91. Signature II showed comparable discrimination. The perioperative decrease in Signature I was greater after R0 than after R1 resection (P = 0.045). In the internal prognostic cohort, high preoperative Signature I was independently associated with shorter overall survival (HR, 2.15; 95% CI, 1.02-4.54) and recurrence-free survival (HR, 2.29; 95% CI, 1.14-4.60). High Signature I also stratified overall and recurrence-free survival in the pooled external cohort (log-rank P = 0.007 and P = 0.004, respectively). Signature I showed consistent diagnostic discrimination across centers and clinically distinct control groups and warrants further evaluation as an adjunct to preoperative assessment of suspected, potentially resectable eCCA. Its perioperative and prognostic associations require prospective confirmation. The incremental value of CA19-9 was context dependent.
